name: go-critic-325d070a-blind26-ots
instr:
# go-critic hands back the wrong advice almost everywhere, without a test suite

We run this tool over our Go sources and read the advice it prints back about each file. That advice has become unreliable in a way that touches nearly everything it looks at: guidance we depend on has gone silent, guidance we never asked for now fires on code that reads fine, and a handful of messages changed wording or now repeat. Nothing about our own code changed and nothing about how we invoke the tool changed. The repository has received 26 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything we could observe from the outside, in the order we tripped over it.

Most of what we noticed is advice that simply stopped arriving. Passing a fat struct to a function by value now produces nothing at all, and neither does ranging over a slice whose elements are large structs, even for perfectly ordinary non-generic types where both remarks were routine before; the run exits cleanly and never mentions how large anything is. Two appends to the same slice, one after the other, are no longer proposed for merging into one call, and a loop that puts every element of one slice onto another an element at a time is no longer proposed as a single spread. A closure whose whole body forwards its arguments to another function is no longer proposed to be replaced by that function itself. A switch holding exactly one case is no longer proposed to be rewritten as an if, while that same proposal now turns up on swi
